newsitem.title: USA: Rain, snow slow Iowa's corn and soybean harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rain, snow slow Iowa's corn and soybean harvest.

text.p: Heavy rain and snow stalled Iowa corn and soybean harvest for about two days but farmers managed to get some crops out of the fields, Iowa's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Soybean harvest was 91 percent complete as of Sunday, up from 83 percent the previous week but below 95 percent for the five-year average.
Corn was 35 percent harvested, against 17 percent last week and 56 percent average.
The moisture level of corn remaining in the field averaged 24 percent while harvested corn moisture averaged 21 percent.
Corn lodging and ear droppage were rated mostly none to light. The crop was rated one percent very poor, three percent poor, 17 percent fair, 57 good and 22 percent excellent.
Winter wheat planting was 88 percent complete as of Sunday, slightly behind the five-year average of 91 percent.
Soil moisture was rated two percent very short, 10 percent short, 76 percent adequate and 12 percent surplus.

Livestock was said to be in good shape but there were a few reports of flu in hogs and calves. Pasture was rated five percent very poor, 18 percent poor, 35 percent fair, 37 percent good and five percent excellent.
